# Redirect to a URL from HTTP request data (Java)

`qualor:java/open-redirect` · Issue · Severity: Medium · [CWE-601](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A01:2021 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Redirects whose target is decided by HTTP request data:

- Servlet: `sendRedirect` and the `Location` header;
- Spring MVC: a `redirect:` view name (returned, or given to a `ModelAndView`), `RedirectView`, and
  a `Location` set on a `ResponseEntity` or `HttpHeaders`;
- Jakarta REST: `seeOther`, `temporaryRedirect`, and a `Location` set on a response builder.

Targets that start with a fixed local path or a fixed origin are not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
A link such as `https://shop.example/login?next=https://evil.example` looks like a link to your
site, but after signing in the user lands on another one. Attackers use this for convincing
phishing pages and to carry tokens from a sign-in flow to a host they control.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the `next` parameter is the whole redirect target.

```java
package com.example.auth;

import java.io.IOException;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServlet;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;

public class AfterLoginServlet extends HttpServlet {
    @Override
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response) throws IOException {
        response.sendRedirect(request.getParameter("next"));
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the parameter only picks one of a few fixed targets.

```java
package com.example.auth;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.Map;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServlet;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import javax.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;

public class AfterLoginServlet extends HttpServlet {
    private static final Map<String, String> TARGETS = Map.of("orders", "/orders", "settings", "/settings");

    @Override
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response) throws IOException {
        response.sendRedirect(TARGETS.getOrDefault(request.getParameter("next"), "/"));
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Redirect only to local paths or to URLs built from a fixed origin: `"/orders/" + id`,
  `"redirect:/orders/" + id`, `BASE_URL + "/orders/" + id`.
- Or map the request value to a target from an allow-list (a `Map.of(...)` of constants or an
  enum).
- A path taken from the request must not start with `//` or `/\`, which browsers read as another
  host.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Jakarta Servlet
- Spring MVC
- Jakarta REST (JAX-RS)

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Conditions are not evaluated: a check that the target is a local path (starts with `/` and not
  `//` or `/\`) does not stop the finding.
- A fixed target is recognised when its text starts with a literal origin followed by `/`, `?` or
  `#`, a local path, a relative path with a separator, or a `static final` or Spring `@Value` base
  followed by such a literal. A host constant in the middle of the string, a `static final` local
  path as the base, `UriComponentsBuilder.fromPath(...)` and a `Location` set in a
  `ResponseEntity` headers lambda are not recognised.
- A handler parameter without an annotation is not a source (the Jakarta REST entity parameter, a
  Spring MVC simple-type parameter), and enum, `List` or `Optional` parameters still count as
  request data.
- Allow-list lookups are recognised only as `Map.of(...)` of constants read with `get` or
  `getOrDefault`, and as `valueOf` of an enum declared in the same file.
<!-- end: known-limits -->
